Gravity Is a Suggestion: 3 Wrestle-Ups to Win the Scramble

A wrestle-up moves you from the ground to your feet.

In Jiu-Jitsu, sweeps are great moves. But rising up is also smart. You stand up fast. You grab a leg. You take top control. Reserve Your Free First Visit.

Safety First on the Mat

  • Train on soft mats. Start slow.
  • Ask a health care pro about knee, hip, or back issues before you drill. Let your coach help you choose a safe move.
  • Focus on smooth movement and calm balance.

Quick Guide: Stay Compact

Keep your frames tight. Move with balance.

Key Rule: Form Over Speed

  • Stay compact: keep limbs close to your core.
  • Load your hips: keep your weight under you.
  • Connect early: secure a grip as you rise.

Pick your situation (jump links)

  • Opponent far away: Combat Base Entry
  • Opponent crowding you: Double-Leg Fold
  • You need an angle: Hip Heist + Drag

1) Opponent Far Away: Combat Base Entry

Best for: when your partner steps back.

Goal: close the gap with steady posture.

Think: Track them down with calm balance.

Steps

  1. Fold and load: fold one leg underneath your hips.
  2. Combat base: bring your heel close. Rise with one knee up.
  3. Knee-walk: take small steps forward on the mat.
  4. Connect: grab a leg as soon as you are close.

Common Mistake and Fix

Mistake: reaching while your hips stay far away.

Fix: move your hips close before you reach.

Mini-drill (30 seconds)

Seated to combat base. Take six small steps forward. Keep your head level and steady.

2) Partner Pressuring In: Double-Leg Fold

Best for: close space when your partner pushes in.

Goal: build a base with tight arm frames.

Think: Stay tight, then drive up.

Steps

  1. Tuck and cover: fold both legs under your hips.
  2. Build the base: rise straight to two knees with good drive.
  3. Hips engaged: keep your hips active and forward.
  4. Hand fight: keep elbows close to ribs. Protect your neck.
  5. Attack: drive for a double leg or front headlock.

Common Mistake and Fix

Mistake: rising with wide open elbows.

Fix: keep elbows glued to your ribs. Look forward.

Mini-drill (10 reps)

Seated to double knees. Posture up tall. Return to seated with calm control. Learn class words.

3) Creating an Angle: Hip Heist and Drag

Best for: creating an angle with an arm drag.

Goal: step around their guard with clear angles. Learn class words.

Think: Good angles beat a heavy base.

Steps

  1. Post strong: place one hand on the mat for support.
  2. Hip heist: lift your hips. Swivel your legs to the side.
  3. Drag: guide their arm across as you rise.
  4. Flank: face their side on your feet.
  5. Finish: secure a leg hold or take their back.

Common Mistake and Fix

Mistake: rising right in front of your partner.

Fix: angle your stance. Lead with your shoulder.

Mini-drill (8 reps per side)

Post your hand. Lift your hips. Swivel and stand at an angle. Keep it smooth.

Troubleshooting: why the transition is defended

Problem Diagnosis Fix
Getting sprawled on Hips too far away Get your heels under your hips before rising
Head getting snapped You are reaching Elbows tight. Post on mat or legs, not the air
Getting stuffed head-on Attacking the center line Use Hip Heist to cut an angle

Solo Mat Drills

Ask your coach to check these drills first. Use mats and a clear space. You can choose these drills as extra practice.

  • The Knee-Walker: Seated to combat base. Take six knee steps. Keep your head level.
  • The Base Builder: Seated to double knees. Posture up. Return to seated. Aim for smooth reps.
  • The Hip Heist: Post your hand. Lift hips. Swivel and stand at an angle.

FAQ

What is a wrestle up in BJJ?

A wrestle-up is rising from the mat to grab a leg and take top control.

Is this the same as standing up?

Both moves help you stand. A stand-up protects your space. A wrestle-up moves forward to take top position.

Do I need shoes for this?

Bare feet work great. These moves are made for the mat. Grip the mat with active toes for drive.
